Mother, daughter among 3 British-Bangladeshis drown in UK beach
item.description:
Three members of a British-Bangladeshi family, including a woman and her teenage daughter, drowned in a beach in Essex of the United Kingdom on Wednesday.
The deceased were identified as Selina Rahman, 42, wife of Sheikh Mansur Rahman, vice-president of the UK chapter of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal, their 15-year-old daughter Samia Rahman, and Musa Ahmed, 9, son of Selina's sister.
Mansur is the son of late Sheikh Mokon Mia, former chairman of Mollargaon Union Parishad in South Surma upazila of Sylhet.
Mansur's brother Sheikh Mahfuzur Rahman Munna said the family met with the tragic accident while visiting West Mersea Beach near Colchester in Essex in the afternoon (local time).
Following the incident, local police, lifeboat crew, a Coastguard helicopter and an air ambulance launched a rescue operation. Despite their efforts, all three were pronounced dead.
Munna said no decision has yet been made on whether the bodies will be brought back to Bangladesh for burial.
According to British media reports, the family had travelled to the seaside to enjoy a summer holiday when the tragedy occurred.
A source familiar with the incident said the accident happened after a high tide swept into the shoreline at West Mersea Beach. The family had been sitting near the water when a young child was caught in the strong current.
Selina and her daughter reportedly rushed into the sea in an attempt to rescue the child but were themselves overwhelmed by the current and drowned.

item.title: Info minister: Authority needed to identify journalists
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Thursday said there is a need for an appropriate authority to determine who qualifies as a journalist and who does not.
The minister made the remarks while delivering a directive speech at the 34th meeting of the Press Accreditation Committee and the inaugural meeting of the newly formed committee, held at the conference room of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting at the Bangladesh Secretariat in the capital.
He advised members of the Press Accreditation Committee to ensure that every decision is consistent with the Constitution, existing laws, and relevant rules and regulations.
He urged them to exercise foresight, wisdom, and adopt an inclusive approach that accommodates the largest possible number of people while making decisions.
He also reminded the committee that its decisions should be broadly acceptable.
The minister said committee members must work not as representatives of any political party but as responsible representatives of a government elected by the people, bearing equal responsibility toward all citizens.
He said the media is a pluralistic sector where there is no alternative to the coexistence of people with diverse opinions, perspectives, and ideas. Therefore, instead of making narrow or biased decisions, the committee should adopt an inclusive approach that accommodates the largest possible number of people.
"The true capability of political leadership lies in making acceptable and inclusive decisions, even in difficult and sensitive situations," the minister said.
Zahir Uddin Swapon said the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting is one of the state's most politically sensitive ministries. Even a minor wrong decision can have major political and social consequences in the future. Therefore, decisions should be made with due consideration of their long-term impact rather than focusing solely on immediate outcomes, he added.
He said the acceptability of the committee's decisions would depend on the wisdom, experience, and foresight of its members.
Principal Information Officer Syed Abdal Ahmed chaired the meeting, which was attended by Secretary (Routine Duty) of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Md Shah Alam, senior ministry officials, and members of the Press Accreditation Committee.

item.title: Muhit: Bangladesh targets eliminating cataract blindness in 5 years
item.description:
State Minister for Health Dr M A Muhit on Thursday expressed optimism that Bangladesh would eliminate cataract blindness within the next four to five years through a coordinated national initiative involving the government, private sector and non-governmental organizations (NGOs).
"A nationwide cataract surgery program will be implemented for elderly citizens, with several hundred thousand successful operations to be carried out annually to eliminate cataract-related blindness within the next four to five years," he said.
He made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at a stakeholder consultation workshop titled "Advanced Eye Care in Bangladesh: Action Plan for Reducing Visual Impairment and Preventing Blindness" at the National Institute of Ophthalmology and Hospital in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital.
An international public health and eye care specialist, Muhit said advanced eye care services powered by artificial intelligence (AI) and modern technology would be expanded to ensure quality treatment reaches poor and marginalized people as a basic citizens' right.
He said Bangladesh has made significant progress in eye care through the combined efforts of the government, private sector and NGOs, but the country still lacks a unified reporting system. To address the issue, he said the government is preparing a five-year national perspective plan incorporating a common reporting mechanism to strengthen eye care services across the country.
Under the plan, the first year will focus on reassessing existing eye care facilities and planning services at district hospitals, followed by measures to improve infrastructure, recruit additional manpower where necessary and enhance service capacity.
The state minister said the government also plans to introduce comprehensive eye care services for people of all age groups.
As part of the initiative, school-based screening programs will be launched to identify vision problems among children and provide corrective glasses, while workers in factories, offices and other institutions will receive regular eye health services and access to spectacles.
Highlighting the growing burden of diabetic retinopathy, Muhit said modern technologies have significantly improved the delivery of eye care services at the grassroots level.
He stressed that advanced eye care services should not remain confined to urban areas but must be made accessible to people living in remote and underserved regions.
Describing the shortage of skilled human resources as a major challenge, the state minister called for greater investment in training and capacity building for ophthalmologists and other eye care professionals.
He also underscored the need to expand both the number and quality of government and private training institutions.
Acting Director of the National Institute of Ophthalmology and Hospital Prof Dr A S M M Quadir also addressed the workshop, while representatives of the ARK Foundation and the World Health Organization (WHO) presented the keynote paper.

item.title: Man awarded death penalty for killing 3rd grader after rape in Comilla
item.description:
A tribunal in Comilla on Thursday sentenced a man to death in a case filed over the rape and murder of a nine-year-old child in Comilla in 2024.
The convict was identified as Mofizul Islam Mofu, son of the late Abdul Khalek of Khilpara village in Comilla Sadar Dakshin Upazila.
Judge Md Yasin Arafat of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal-1 delivered the verdict after completing the trial in just 19 working days.
According to the prosecution, on April 29, 2024, Tanjim Sultana Jhumur, a third-grade student at Sonali Shishu Bidyaniketan in Kheyaish village under Galiara Union of Comilla Sadar Dakshin Upazila, went missing while returning home from school.
When she failed to return home at the expected time, her family searched for her in every possible place. On information from local residents, they later recovered Jhumur's body from a paddy field in the Thakurbari area of the village.
Police also recovered her school bag, school uniform, and shoes from the spot.
The following day, the victim's mother, Razia Akhter, filed a case with Sadar Dakshin Police Station, naming Mofizul Islam Mofu, a resident of Khilpara village in Sadar Dakshin Upazila, as the sole accused.
Three days after the incident, members of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) conducted a raid in Chandpur and arrested the accused, Mofizul Islam Mofu.
Later, Mofizul confessed to raping and killing the child before the court.

item.title: Khalilur urges stronger regional cooperation for Rohingya solution
item.description:
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman has urged Asean Regional Forum (ARF) members to strengthen regional cooperation and collectively support efforts to secure a sustainable solution to the protracted Rohingya crisis.
Addressing the 33rd Asean Regional Forum Ministerial Meeting in Manila, Rahman reaffirmed Bangladesh’s steadfast commitment to dialogue, multilateralism and a rules-based international order amid growing geopolitical and regional security challenges, said a foreign ministry press release on Thursday.
Highlighting Bangladesh’s humanitarian burden, the foreign minister said the country has been hosting more than 1.3 million forcibly displaced Rohingyas from Myanmar for nearly a decade.
He warned that the prolonged crisis has exposed Bangladesh to an array of transborder crimes, including drug trafficking, human trafficking and illicit flows of arms and weapons, posing wider regional security concerns.
“Rohingyas are not stateless people by circumstance; they are stateless by design. It is a political failure, and demands a political solution,” Rahman said.
He called upon ARF participants to collectively support efforts to create conditions in Myanmar conducive to safe, voluntary, dignified and sustainable repatriation of the Rohingyas to their homeland in Rakhine State.
The foreign minister said the international community is confronting unprecedented geopolitical challenges and stressed that sustained dialogue and diplomacy remain the most effective means of addressing emerging global and regional security concerns.
He urged all states to exercise maximum restraint in dealing with maritime disputes, uphold international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and resolve differences through peaceful dialogue.
Addressing climate-related security challenges, Rahman said Bangladesh, as one of the countries most vulnerable to climate change and natural disasters, remains committed to advancing regional cooperation in disaster preparedness and early warning systems.
In its capacity as Co-Chair of the ARF Inter-Sessional Meeting on Disaster Relief, Bangladesh would continue advocating stronger regional resilience under the ARF framework, he said.
Rahman also highlighted both the opportunities and risks associated with artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, calling for closer regional cooperation to counter cybersecurity threats, disinformation and misuse of advanced technologies.
He proposed exploring a regional technology governance framework tailored to the region’s unique geopolitical and developmental realities.
The foreign minister also expressed appreciation for the support extended by participating countries to Bangladesh’s candidature for the presidency of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
Reaffirming Bangladesh’s commitment to stronger regional cooperation based on mutual respect and shared prosperity, Rahman said: “Bangladesh will always choose dialogue over division, partnership over polarization.”

item.title: State minister urges BIWTA to boost revenue, improve services
item.description:
State Minister for Shipping Md Razib Ahsan on Thursday directed the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA) to further intensify its activities to improve service quality, expand revenue collection and make the country's inland water transport system more modern, safe and efficient. The directive came at a view-exchange meeting on "Enhancing the Authority's Revenue Generation and Service Improvement," held at the sixth-floor conference room of BIWTA's head office, with Ministry of Shipping Secretary Zakaria also present.
Mohidul Islam, Additional Secretary to the government and Chairman of BIWTA, opened the meeting with a PowerPoint presentation on the authority's revenue and income growth, service improvement measures and ongoing development activities, touching on dredging operations, maintenance of river navigability, river port management, leasing activities, revenue collection, ensuring water safety and digital transformation of services.
Following the presentation, the state minister issued a series of directions aimed at making BIWTA's operations more result-oriented and people-friendly.
He asked the authority to carry out dredging in a cost-effective manner, prioritising routes most in need of excavation, and to take up projects to make buoys, lights, beacons and navigational markers more visible across waterways to enhance safety of movement.
He also instructed BIWTA's Port Division to give special priority to quickly settling ghats that remain unresolved in leasing up to the seventh phase of the 2026-27 fiscal year, and called for updating foreshore and land-use fees to boost revenue alongside effective steps to expedite civil suits related to ghats and points.
The state minister further directed the authority to introduce automation in cargo loading and unloading at river ports in phases, take coordinated measures with all relevant stakeholders to ensure the safety of vessels plying the waterways, and identify potential new revenue sectors for the Port Division with quickly implementable initiatives.
Speakers at the meeting said BIWTA needs to be transformed into a more efficient, modern, technology-driven and service-oriented institution in line with the government's Smart Bangladesh vision, stressing the need to create new avenues for revenue generation while ensuring optimal use of existing resources.
The state minister and the secretary, at the end of the meeting, expressed hope that swift implementation of the directions would help BIWTA enhance service quality, expand revenue collection, ensure navigational safety and make the country's inland water transport system more effective and people-friendly.

item.title: ULAB scool of business concludes BBA Monsoon Expo 2026
item.description:
The ULAB School of Business (USB) successfully wrapped up its signature three-day BBA Monsoon Expo 2026 on Wednesday with a vibrant closing ceremony held at the main campus. Organized under the university's flagship Curriculum Integration Program for the Summer 2026 term, the expo celebrated the intersection of student-led academic innovation and seasonal radiance. The initiative brought real-world industry applications directly into the classroom environment across multiple foundational business courses.
The competitive expo featured extensive student engagement, drawing in around 300 students divided into roughly 35 innovative teams. An elite panel of judges evaluated the participants throughout the exhibition. The panel ultimately recognized 13 exceptional teams for their outstanding final projects and professional presentations. Winners were chosen based on rigorous criteria, including core project depth, exceptional teamwork skills, and inventive problem-solving.
The program cross-integrated multiple business pathways, highlighting critical core courses and specialized supply chain tracks. Dedicated faculty members guided the participating cohorts. The event also held a Corporate Monsoon Flashmob led by ULAB students with a Tagore song on its beautiful open campus.
The closing ceremony concluded with an inspiring corporate address titled "The Economy of Monsoon" delivered by Professor Milan Kumar Bhattacharjee, PhD, special adviser to the Board of Trustees and Treasurer at ULAB. Professor Sarwar Uddin Ahmed, dean School of Business delivered a speech and the event ended with a celebratory certificate distribution, an academic photoshoot, and a vote of thanks from Dr Wazir Ahmad, director of the BBA Program.

item.title: Infant killing: Police seek remand for father, hearing Sunday
item.description:
Police have sought a three-day remand for Kabir Islam, the father accused of killing his seven-month-old daughter by throwing her to the ground during a domestic dispute with his wife in Dhaka's Uttara area.
The remand petition was submitted on Thursday by the case's investigating officer and Sub-Inspector Mehedi Hasan Faisal of Turag Police Station.
Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Zakir Hossain fixed Sunday for the hearing on the remand petition in the presence of the accused.
SI Helal Uddin of the prosecution division confirmed the matter.
According to the case documents, Kabir allegedly slammed his seven-month-old daughter, Rafa Moni Kobita, onto the ground on the evening of July 15 following an argument with his wife. Locals caught him and handed him over to police.
The following day, police produced him before the court after showing him arrested under Section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, and the court ordered that he be sent to jail.
The infant succumbed to her injuries while undergoing treatment on July 16.
On July 17, the child's maternal grandmother, Sarmin Akter, filed a murder case with Turag Police Station against Kabir. Police later sought to show him arrested in the murder case, and the court granted the application on Tuesday before sending him back to jail.
According to the case statement, Kabir and Lima Akter were married two years ago, and Rafa Moni was their only child. Kabir, a rickshaw puller by profession, had allegedly been addicted to drugs for a long time.
The complaint alleges that Kabir frequently assaulted and verbally abused his wife after taking drugs. On July 15, Lima had gone to her father's home in Balur Math Harun Molla Basti with the baby to visit her ailing father.
Around 7:00 pm, an argument broke out between the couple over a family matter. Enraged, Kabir allegedly snatched the infant from her grandmother's arms, lifted her above his head, and hurled her onto the road.
The critically injured child was rushed to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where she later died while receiving treatment.

item.title: ICT shows Mozzafar arrested in crimes against humanity case
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Thursday showed Major (retd) Mozzafar Hossain, an accused in the assassination case of former President Ziaur Rahman, arrested in crimes against humanity case over atrocities allegedly committed in Feni during the July mass uprising. The tribunal also granted investigators two days to interrogate him.
A three-member bench of ICT-2, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, passed the order following a prosecution petition.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam appeared for the prosecution and sought permission to show Mozzafar arrested in the case, allow a two-day interrogation, and extend the deadline for submitting the investigation report.
After the hearing, the tribunal granted the prosecution's petition, formally showing Mozzafar arrested in the case and authorising investigators to interrogate him for two days at a time convenient to the investigation agency. The tribunal also fixed September 23 for the submission of the investigation report.
Mozzafar was produced before the tribunal earlier in the day and will remain in custody at the Dhaka Cantonment prison.
Lieutenant General (Retd.) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, another accused in the same case, was also produced before the tribunal.
According to the prosecution, evidence collected during the investigation suggests Mozzafar's involvement in various crimes against humanity during the Awami League government's tenure. Prosecutors alleged that he maintained regular communication with Masud Uddin Chowdhury during the killings in Feni amid the July mass uprising, leading to the application to show him arrested in the case.
On July 21, the prosecution sought a production warrant for Mozzafar, one of the accused in the Ziaur Rahman assassination case. After evading arrest for nearly 45 years, he was apprehended from a residence in Dhaka's Banani area on the night of July 15 and handed over to the Military Police at Dhaka Cantonment the following day.

item.title: Budget's success depends on implementation, says Khasru
item.description:
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury on Thursday said the true success of the budget depends on its effective implementation, urging officials of the Finance Division to work collectively to translate the fiscal blueprint into tangible outcomes.
Speaking at his first meeting with Finance Division officials at the Ministry of Finance, the minister said the budget, prepared through nearly two months of work, has received appreciation from people across the country.
“A well-prepared budget alone is not enough. Its real success depends on effective implementation,” he said.
Khasru expressed confidence that the Finance Division will be able to implement the budget through coordinated efforts.
Finance Division Secretary Dr Khairuzzaman Mozumder chaired the meeting.
The minister also called for changing the negative public perception of bureaucracy, saying he has realised over the past four months that any challenge could be overcome through teamwork.
He urged officials to move away from conventional approaches and embrace innovative thinking to keep pace with a rapidly changing world.
Khasru said official meetings should not remain one way, stressing the need to encourage open and spontaneous participation of officers.
He called for a work culture based on free discussion, mutual cooperation and “out-of-the-box” thinking, adding that the workplace should function like a family where officials focus on solutions instead of merely identifying problems.
The minister said objective and timely feedback from different wings of the Finance Division will facilitate better policy-making and decision-making.
Describing the Finance Division as the centre of the country’s economic management, he urged all officials to discharge their responsibilities with professionalism and dedication in the national interest.
Later, speaking to reporters after a meeting at the Secretariat on the integrated development plan for Cox’s Bazar, the minister said the government has initiated steps to prepare a comprehensive master plan to develop the coastal district into an international and regional tourism hub.
He said the government is also reviewing the long-standing 50 metre and 500 metre development restrictions in coastal areas to facilitate planned tourism infrastructure while ensuring environmental protection.
“Where tourism is developed, hotels, motels, resorts and recreational facilities will have to be established. Development opportunities must be created without compromising environmental conservation,” Khosru said.
He said the government has a broader vision for Cox’s Bazar, highlighting ongoing infrastructure projects, including the construction of an international airport, railway connectivity and improved road links from Chattogram.
The minister said these projects will be integrated to transform Cox’s Bazar into a modern digital tourism city.
He also said Bangladesh’s target of becoming a $1 trillion economy by 2034 will be supported by Cox’s Bazar as one of the country’s major growth hubs through the expansion of tourism, trade and service sectors.

item.title: Narendra Modi facing the biggest youth protest movement of his rule, the Cockroach Janta Party
item.description:
Under the oppressive heat of monsoon rain, thousands of young Indians flooded New Delhi in a battle for accountability and their futures.
As politicians returned to the capital this week, waves of protesters attempted to march to parliament before police and paramilitary forces fired tear gas and sound cannons and used batons to break up crowds.
Rather than quell the dissent, the show of force from authorities has spurred defiance across the country and the world.
From Mumbai and Goa to London and New York, young Indians have taken to the streets, showing the power of the world’s largest youth population.
At the centre is Abhijeet Dipke, a 30-year-old student who is fast becoming the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 12-year reign.
On May 16, 2026, Mr Dipke founded the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth movement that launched on social media after remarks made by one of India’s most senior judges.
In May, Supreme Court Chief Justice Surya Kant described unemployed young people as “cockroaches.”
“There are youngsters like cockroaches. They don’t get any employment. They don’t have any place in a profession,” Justice Kant said.
The comments struck a nerve with Mr Dipke, who was studying in Boston, Massachusetts, at the time.
That post received engagement levels in the millions.
He then started a CJP Instagram page and within a day more than 1 million people had followed that account.
Within four days that number had reached 10 million.
Today the account has almost 25 million followers.
“That is when I realized that there is some genuine frustration among the youth regarding unemployment and regarding the irregularities in the examination system of India,” Mr Dipke told 7.30.
“This frustration and this disappointment have been there for quite some years now, and clearly they have given up on all existing political parties.”
Mr Dipke has now crossed into a role he never imagined, taking on one of the world’s most powerful governments.
“I have never been that person who used to socialize much. But now I’m a public face where I have to constantly meet people, greet them.
“This is a whole new ball game for me.”
The formation of the CJP coincided with a wave of corruption allegations, after the results of the fiercely competitive national medical entrance examination were cancelled after questions were leaked. It forced about 2 million students to sit the test again.
There were 20 student suicides in the wake of the cancelled results. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan has been blamed.
Youth unemployment has become one of India’s most politically sensitive issues, hitting 40 per cent for graduates aged under 25.
Government jobs remain highly coveted because they offer stable, lifelong employment, but competition for them is fierce.
Many protesters say opportunities have become increasingly difficult to secure, while repeated exam controversies have eroded trust in the system.
For more than a month, protesters have staged a sit-in at Delhi’s designated protest site, Jantar Mantar, demanding Mr Pradhan resign.
A permit is required to protest at Jantar Mantar and usually demonstrators must leave by 5pm or risk arrest. However the CJP has been allowed to stay in a move some experts say shows the government has recognized the need to keep young people on side.
The CJP’s presence in other areas has not been completely without opposition though.
The government shut down the group’s social media accounts early on, accusing the group of posing a threat to national security, before a court allowed them to be restored.
Most support for the CJP had been online until last weekend. That changed on Saturday when the Delhi High Court ruled the government was responsible for the welfare of activist Sonam Wungchuk.
Mr Wungchuk was 20 days into a hunger strike in support of students. He was picked up and forcibly removed to a hospital on Saturday, sparking an outpouring of anger from India’s youth.
It triggered thousands of people, some from hundreds of kilometers away, to make the journey to New Delhi in support of Mr Wungchuk and the CJP.
Gaurav Ujale travelled more than six hours from his village in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh to join Monday’s protest
“We are here with the hope that the system will change,” he said.
As thousands attempted to march towards parliament, police blocked roads, fired tear gas and smoke bombs and dragged demonstrators away.
The CJP said about 150 protesters were taken to the hospital with injuries including lacerations to the head and broken bones, and dozens were detained.
Delhi Police said almost 120 officers were injured.
Despite the clashes, Mr Dipke has repeatedly urged supporters to remain peaceful, even intervening when protesters have begun chanting violent slogans about Mr Modi.
Author and political journalist Ruhi Tewari said the government underestimated the movement in its early days.
“Instead of addressing the issue and nipping it in the bud, it’s allowed it to balloon into this huge, massive movement that is catching national attention,” Tewari said.
Ms Tewari said India had not faced a protest movement of this size in more than a decade, which meant the government now faced a dilemma. Backing down risks appearing weak, but ignoring the protests risks mobilizing more young voters.
“It’s really boxed itself into a bit of a corner,” she said.
After Monday’s violence the government began engaging with CJP leaders.
India Health Minister JP Nadda promised to consider the group’s demands, and the education minister posted on X, announcing the government remained committed to addressing young people’s concerns.
Whether the movement can force lasting political change remains uncertain, according to Tewari.
The CJP is not a registered political party and cannot contest elections, which she says limits its ability to directly challenge the BJP at the ballot box.
Mr Dipke disagrees.
“There’s a great power in social movements, but if we have to start a political party just to seek accountability from the government, then that’s a very wrong idea,” he said.

item.title: UN demands probe into killing of Malian soldiers
item.description:
The United Nations on Thursday demanded an investigation into the killing of at least 50 Malian soldiers in an attack by Tuareg separatists and jihadists.
The attack on the army convoy leaving the strategic northern town of Anefis occurred on Saturday, following weeks of fighting with both sides attempting to take control.
In early July, fighters from the Tuareg separatist Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) and the Al-Qaeda-affiliated Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (Jnim) briefly captured the town and encircled a military base used by the Malian army and Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps.
The Jnim and the FLA claimed responsibility for the attack.
“We deplore the reported torture and killing of dozens of surrendering Malian soldiers by the Tuareg-led FLA and the Jnim armed groups,” UN human rights office spokesman Thameen Al-Kheetan said in a statement.
“There needs to be a thorough and independent investigation into the circumstances of this incident, including the actions contained in the horrendous footage circulated online appearing to show FLA/Jnim members firing at the soldiers after they surrendered, with their hands behind their heads.”
Mali has been ruled by a military government since back-to-back coups in 2020 and 2021.
The junta has struggled to deliver on its promise to restore security after years of jihadist and separatist unrest.
“Killing, torturing or abusing individuals hors de combat is a war crime. The armed groups must stop such violations and prevent any recurrence,” said Kheetan.
“Accountability must be achieved, and those responsible must be brought to justice within fair trials. Remedy must be provided to victims and their families.”

item.title: UK withdraws remaining diplomats from Iran
item.description:
Britain said on Thursday it had withdrawn remaining diplomatic staff from Iran as the conflict between Iran and the United States escalates.
“Due to the security situation, UK staff have been temporarily withdrawn from Iran. Our embassy continues to operate remotely,” the Foreign Office said on its website.
Britain in June withdrew its embassy staff from Iran, following in the footsteps of other European nations as well as Australia and New Zealand.
The withdrawals came after Israel launched renewed air strikes on Iran claiming its arch enemy was on the verge of developing a nuclear weapon.
The Foreign Office (FCDO) declined to say how many staff had been withdrawn, after a similar move in February.
The FCDO “advises against all travel to Iran. If you are a British national already in Iran, either resident or visitor, carefully consider your presence there and the risks you take by staying,” it says on its website.
British couple Craig Foreman and his wife Lindsay were detained while travelling in Iran during a round-the-world motorbike trip at the start of 2025.
They are serving a 10-year sentence for spying - charges they both deny. Their family said last week that Craig Foreman had been given an extra two years for talking to the media.

item.title: Deadly wildfires force thousands from homes in parts of Europe
item.description:
Wildfires continued to sweep across swathes of Italy, France and Spain on Thursday, forcing thousands to flee blazes fanned by scorching temperatures and strong winds.
Three firefighters have been killed fighting the flames as southern Europe endures another spell of severe heat, with temperatures topping 40°C in some areas.
Although the summer of 2026 is only halfway through, it already ranks as the second largest EU area burned by wildfires over the last 20 years, according to European satellite data from the Effis system analyzed by AFP.
“We saw a big cloud of black smoke spread across the sky in the middle of the afternoon,” said Julie Leonard, a Bordeaux resident in her thirties who had to seek shelter from a major fire around Le Porge in south-west France.
In Sicily, around 6,000 firefighters, forest guards and civil protection officials battled dozens of fires raging for days across the Italian Mediterranean island despite the deployment of water-bombing aircraft.
A firefighter died after falling ill while battling the flames, the interior minister said.
A spokesperson for Italy’s Civil Protection Agency told AFP the situation in Sicily was “serious” and that the fires were “being fueled by very high temperatures and very dry soil.”
More than 160 fires have also been recorded in the neighboring Calabria region, with the local civil protection chief blaming arsonists who allegedly tied rags soaked in flammable liquid to the tails of stray cats to spread the flames.
In France, more than 10,000 tourists evacuated camping sites and other holiday accommodation near Bordeaux in the southwest on Thursday, as a wildfire ravaged a seaside pine forest.
The blaze in Le Porge had ripped through 2,400 hectares (5,900 acres) -- an area twice the size of London’s Heathrow airport -- since Wednesday, officials said.
No homes had been destroyed and no casualties reported, but two firefighters died on Tuesday tackling another blaze near Bordeaux airport.
“We’re dealing with a very dense stand of closely packed pines,” firefighter Captain Wilfried Schneider told AFP, describing a fire of “rare” intensity.
“If I’d been brave, I would have stayed in my cabin, but it was too hot. I got in my car and left,” said Bernard Roche, 75, who has lived in the area for 35 years.
Le Porge Mayor Martial Zaninetti said the fire appeared to have been sparked by a brush-clearing machine, though police were still investigating the cause.
Skies over Le Porge turned orange as smoke rose from charred and still-crackling pine trees, AFP journalists reported, while helicopters made repeated runs over evacuated neighborhoods.
Fires in 2022 damaged 30,000 hectares of the same forest, forcing some 50,000 people to be evacuated.
Fires are breaking out faster because climate change, caused by the burning of oil, coal and gas, is making a European drought more severe, climatologists from the World Weather Attribution group said in a study published on Thursday.
Across the border in Spain, progress against a major wildfire south of Madrid allowed most residents to return, emergency services said Thursday.
The blaze, which broke out Wednesday near the city of Toledo, prompted authorities to evacuate several districts as flames advanced towards homes. Villagers in El Encinar del Alberche were still being urged to stay away.
Firefighters described overnight efforts as “very positive”, although the blaze had not yet been stabilized and several roads remained closed.
But hundreds of firefighters were still battling a much larger wildfire in Guadalajara province, north of Madrid, which has burnt about 32,000 hectares since it started last Thursday.
“Climate change is what kills, what destroys our villages and our natural and cultural heritage,” civil protection chief Virginia Barcones told Spanish radio, warning some fires become so intense that, despite the deployment of aircraft and ground crews, firefighters stand “no chance.”
Barcones said conditions at the Guadalajara blaze were improving but warned of strong winds and extreme heat later on Thursday.
Madrid emergency services also warned of an “extreme” wildfire risk as Spain endured the final day of a heatwave. Spain’s weather agency Aemet said temperatures were expected to ease this weekend before likely rising again.

item.title: Jamaat formally notifies EC of Satkhira-4 MP Nazrul's expulsion
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Thursday formally notified the Election Commission (EC) that it has expelled Satkhira-4 lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam from the party after an internal investigation found allegations of moral turpitude against him to be true.
In a letter signed by the party's Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar and addressed to Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) AMM Nasir Uddin, Jamaat informed the EC of its decision.
According to the letter, the party conducted an organizational investigation into various media reports published recently regarding MP Nazrul.
The investigation found the allegations of moral turpitude against him to be substantiated. Consequently, he was expelled from the party under Article 62 of the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami constitution, it said.
The letter stated that the decision was unanimously taken at an emergency meeting of the party's Central Executive Council held on Wednesday chaired by Jamaat Ameer and Leader of the Opposition Dr Shafiqur Rahman.
It said copies of the decision have also been sent to the Office of the speaker of the National Parliament for taking necessary action.

item.title: Bangladesh to play one-off Test against England at Lord's
item.description:
The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has confirmed that England will host Bangladesh for a one-off Test at Lord's Cricket Ground next year.
The match, scheduled to begin on May 28, 2027, will mark Bangladesh's first Test tour of England since the two-match series in 2010.
The ECB also announced that the England Women's team will conclude their home summer with a three-match Vitality IT20 series and a three-match Metro Bank ODI series against Bangladesh Women.
"We are excited to welcome Bangladesh Men for a one-off Test at Lord's, which will be the first time we have played them at home in a Test since 2010, while also hosting Bangladesh Women in a white-ball series," ECB Chief Executive Officer Richard Gould said while confirming Bangladesh's schedule.
Although Bangladesh lost both Tests during their 2010 tour of England, the series featured memorable individual performances.
Current Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) president Tamim Iqbal scored a century at Lord's, earning a place on the prestigious Lord's Honours Board. Fast bowler Shahadat Hossain also secured a place on the Honours Board after claiming a five-wicket haul during the tour.

item.title: Klopp expected to be named new Germany coach on Friday
item.description:
Jurgen Klopp is widely expected to formally take over as the new head coach of the German men's national football team, with the German Football Association (DFB) calling a press conference for Friday.
Klopp, famed for his success during stints as coach at Borussia Dortmund and especially Liverpool, has been in talks with the DFB about trying to lead Germany -- long a football powerhouse -- back to prominence.
On Thursday, the DFB invited the media to a press conference on Friday morning at 11am (0900GMT) at its Frankfurt headquarters, without specifying the topic.
That is because the DFB's governing bodies have not yet met to formally approve the deal with Klopp, according to reports from AFP's sports subsidiary SID.
Klopp, 59, is among the most decorated football coaches of his generation and is expected to sign a contract with Germany that runs until 2030, the date of the next World Cup.
Since 2025, Klopp has been under contract with Austrian energy drink maker Red Bull as "Head of Global Soccer", where he oversees the football clubs affiliated with the company such as RB Leipzig, Red Bull Salzburg and the New York Red Bulls.
According to German media reports Red Bull will release Klopp from his deal without a transfer fee, instead accepting a million-euro ($1.1 million) donation to Red Bull's Wings for Life charity foundation, which supports research into spinal cord injuries.
The DFB dismissed former head coach Julian Nagelsmann after Germany crashed out of this summer's World Cup in disappointing fashion, losing to Paraguay on penalties in the round of 32.
That means the German men's team has suffered three straight World Cup debacles since winning their fourth title in 2014.
Germany made first-round exits in both 2018 and 2022. They have won just one knockout match at the past five major tournaments, reaching the quarter-finals as hosts at Euro 2024.
Klopp had successful coaching tenures at German clubs Mainz -- where he was a player for more than a decade -- and Dortmund.
He then became a legend at Liverpool, where he coached the English side to a league title in 2020 -- ending a 30-year drought. He also led the club to a Champions League triumph, their sixth European crown.
Citing fatigue, Klopp stepped down from the Liverpool job in 2024.

item.title: Norway set to make formal complaint to FIFA over Balogun red card saga
item.description:
Norway's football chief told The Times they are set to make a formal complaint to FIFA over the suspension of Folarin Balogun's World Cup ban because it has put "the whole game at risk".
Lise Klaveness, the president of the Norwegian Football Federation (NFF), says she will seek the backing of her board to lodge the complaint with FIFA's ethics committee over an incident that "should not have happened".
The NFF have already formally complained over FIFA president Gianni Infantino awarding football's governing body's inaugural Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump, which was widely ridiculed.
"I will bring it to a board meeting and discuss with my board, and then we do it," Klaveness told The Times in an interview published on Thursday.
"To me, it should be in the same sphere of ethical complaint."
Trump's involvement in the Balogun affair sparked the controversy.
Balogun's red card in the last-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina resulted in an automatic suspension for the match with Belgium.
But FIFA stepped in and suspended his ban, leading to widespread condemnation, especially when it emerged that Trump had intervened by phoning Infantino.
Belgium appeared inspired by the row and thrashed the co-hosts 4-1.
"When you bend a rule like this, you're on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk," said Klaveness.
"It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game.
"First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it.
"We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process."
"We need our leader in FIFA to say that this was an error," she added.
- 'Under the carpet' -
Klaveness, a former Norway international who has been head of the NFF since 2022, said bending over for a head of state was a dangerous precedent.
"If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behaviour and the organisation's behaviour, and also the red line of what states' leaders should interfere with," she said.
"And that happened."
Klaveness was unimpressed too that, according to The Times, the decision to suspend the ban had been taken solely by by the chairman of FIFA's disciplinary committee, Mohammad al-Kamali, who did not consult the other members.
"When you make controversial decisions, and when there has been an external, very powerful voice in your ear, it's very important that you have more voices (making the decision)," she said.
"And if you don't, it's a mistake."
Klaveness said the issue could not just be laid to rest and forgotten about.
"To try to sweep this under the carpet now will not fly," the 45-year-old lawyer said.
"Too many felt this... coaches, players, fans... that this was too close to the game."
Klaveness, who says she is not a contender to take on Infantino in the presidential election next year, is equally critical of the proposal by South America to increase the finals from 48 to 64 teams.
Norway enjoyed a successful return to the finals after a 28-year hiatus, losing to England in the quarter-finals.
"Smaller nations like ourselves, that haven't been there for 20 years, showed the World Cup could be extended to 48 teams," said Klaveness.
"It's not in football's interest, or even reasonable, to now start to talk about 64 teams -- 48 teams was a big change.
"If you bring the discussion now to 64, and powerful people say it, you will create distrust.
"The World Cup should not interfere with the domestic leagues, or the confederations, more than it does today."

item.title: Asian Games: Bangladesh drawn with Korea Republic, DPR Korea and Myanmar
item.description:
Bangladesh national women's football team has been drawn in Group B alongside Korea Republic, DPR Korea and Myanmar for the 20th Asian Games, which will be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4.
The official draw for the women's football tournament was held on Thursday in Japan, with the 12 participating teams divided into three groups.
The matches will be played from September 14 to October 2. The top two teams from each group, along with the two best third-placed teams, will qualify for the quarter-finals.
Bangladesh have previously competed only once in the Asian Games women's football tournament. At the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games in China, the women in red and green were eliminated in the group stage after registering one draw and two defeats in three matches.

item.title: Mercantile Bank, PKSF sign credit guarantee agreement
item.description:
Mercantile Bank PLC has officially signed an agreement with the Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) to avail credit guarantee services under the Credit Enhancement Scheme (CES).
The signing ceremony was graced by Md Fazlul Kader, managing director of PKSF, along with Md Zakir Hossain, deputy managing director & chief risk officer (CRO) of Mercantile Bank, and Farid Ahmed, EVP & head of the bank’s Gulshan branch.
Under this strategic partnership, Mercantile Bank will extend credit and loan facilities to PKSF-enlisted partner organizations covered under the Credit Enhancement Scheme.
These loan disbursements will be fully backed by the credit guarantee facilities provided by PKSF, significantly lowering lending risks and boosting financial resources for small businesses.
This joint initiative aims to reinforce micro-enterprise financing across Bangladesh by safely channeling banking sector funds into rural, low-income, and marginalized communities.

item.title: Home loan interest rates and your CIBIL Score: what a jump from 680 to 750 actually saves you
item.description:
Your CIBIL Score is one of the factors lenders consider when deciding your home loan interest rates. A score of 725 or above is generally considered strong for a home loan application. Moving from a score of 680 to 750 does not guarantee a fixed rate drop, but it can improve your approval prospects and may reduce the rate a lender offers you. On a Rs. 50 lakh home loan over 20 years, even a 0.50% difference in rate can change your total interest outgo by several lakhs.
Bajaj Finance offers home loans of up to Rs. 15 crore* at interest rates starting from 7.25%* p.a., with repayment tenures up to 32 years*. This article covers how lenders assess your score, what a score improvement can realistically change, and how to apply when you're ready.
A CIBIL Score is a three-digit number, ranging from 300 to 900, that reflects your credit history. It is calculated by TransUnion CIBIL based on your repayment behaviour, outstanding debt, and credit age.
Lenders use this score as one data point when deciding whether to approve your home loan and at what interest rate. A higher score signals a lower credit risk to the lender. However, a high score alone does not guarantee the lowest available rate.
Home loan interest rates are set after lenders assess your complete financial profile. Your score influences the decision, but it is not the only variable in the equation.

item.title: Al-Arafah Islami Bank holds discussion with Hajj agency representatives
item.description:
To ensure convenient, secure and timely banking services for Hajj pilgrims and strengthen coordination between the bank and Hajj agencies, Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC, organized a "Discussion Meeting on Hajj Management."
The discussion meeting was held at a hotel in Dhaka on July 22.
Secretary of the Ministry of Religious Affairs Munshi Alauddin Al Azad, attended the event as chief guest, while President of the Hajj Agencies Association of Bangladesh (Haab) Syed Golam Sarwar was present as special guest.
The program was presided over by the bank's managing director Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan.
Among others present at the event were the bank's deputy managing directors Md Fazlur Rahman Chowdhury, Md Aminul Islam Bhuiyan, SM Abu Jafar, and Syed Abul Hashem, along with senior executives of the bank, branch managers, and representatives of Hajj agencies from across the country.
In his address, Munshi Alauddin Al Azad said that close coordination among the government, banks and Hajj agencies is essential to ensure convenient, secure and uninterrupted services for Hajj pilgrims.
He appreciated Al-Arafah Islami Bank's initiative to make Hajj management more efficient, transparent and customer-friendly through technology-driven banking services.
Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan said that ensuring reliable and timely banking services for Hajj pilgrims is one of the top priorities of Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC.
He noted that the bank has integrated technology, operational excellence and customer-centric services into its Hajj banking solutions to keep pace with evolving customer needs.
He further reaffirmed the Bank's commitment to providing comprehensive support at every stage of the Hajj journey and continuously enhancing service standards to earn the trust and satisfaction of Hajj pilgrims.
The meeting featured interactive discussions on further improving banking services for Hajj pilgrims.
Participants emphasized the importance of strengthening collaboration among all stakeholders involved in Hajj management, expanding technology-enabled banking solutions and ensuring faster, more efficient and seamless services for Hajj pilgrims.

Stentorian releases new single 'Opekhar Shesh Prohor'
item.description:
Bangladeshi heavy metal band Stentorian has released "Opekhar Shesh Prohor," its latest single following the comeback track "Chaya Britto."
The song explores the final moments of waiting, capturing the emotions of uncertainty, acceptance, hope, loss, resilience, and courage through the band's signature heavy metal sound.
"Opekhar Shesh Prohor" combines heavy guitar riffs, melodic arrangements, cinematic elements, and emotionally driven songwriting.
The track features drummer Mehmood Afridi Tony, whose performance adds energy and precision, while guitarist and producer Wasiun Khan contributes a guest guitar solo.
The accompanying music video follows a solitary character through themes of memory, longing, perseverance, and self-discovery using symbolic storytelling.
With the new release, Stentorian continues its return with a focus on artistic growth, creative collaboration, and its commitment to heavy metal.
Stentorian's current lineup features Torsha Khan on lead vocals, James Kabir on guitar, synthesizers, keyboards, and backing vocals, Tutul Rashid on guitar, and Shams Alim Biswas on bass guitar. The single also features guest performances by acclaimed drummer Mehmood Afridi Tony and guitarist Wasiun Khan, who contributed the song's guitar solo.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 805 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Thursday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 805.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified both of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 710, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 95, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Of the two new suspected fatalities, one was reported in the Sylhet division and the other in the Rangpur division. At the district level, the deaths occurred in Sunamganj and Gaibandha, with one casualty reported in each.
A total of 848 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Thursday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 121,200.
During the same period, 166 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 15,007.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 103,863 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 100,188 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

US House passes symbolic resolution calling for Trump to halt Iran war
item.description:
The US House of Representatives passed a largely symbolic resolution Thursday calling for President Donald Trump to halt military action against Iran, delivering another congressional rebuke as the Middle East war sharply escalates.

The measure -- which passed 214-208 after four Republicans joined opposition Democrats in support -- directs Trump to remove US forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress explicitly authorizes the war.

But as a concurrent resolution, it does not go to the president for signature and carries disputed legal force, meaning Trump is almost certain to ignore it.

The vote came after the United States launched a fresh wave of strikes on Iranian military targets, its 12th consecutive night of attacks, while Iran has fired on US bases and American-allied Gulf states.

Four US service personnel killed in recent Iran-related attacks were honored this week as their remains returned to the United States in flag-draped cases.

The conflict has also spread further across regional shipping lanes. Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said Wednesday they had struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea after declaring a maritime blockade, while Iran has kept pressure on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global energy supplies.

The House vote underscored growing unease in Congress over a war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February and has become a political burden for Republicans ahead of November''s midterm elections.
Democratic congresswoman Pramila Jayapal said the war had "no clear mission, no strategy, no end goal."

Democrats have used repeated war powers votes to force Republicans onto the record over the unpopular conflict, arguing that Trump violated the Constitution by launching and sustaining military operations without approval from Congress.

Most Republicans, however, stood by the president.

House Foreign Affairs Committee chairman Brian Mast accused critics of failing to recognize the sacrifice of US troops killed in the conflict and said the operation was bringing a "reckoning" for Iranian attacks.

The Senate was voting Thursday on a separate war powers measure from Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen. It was expected to fail.

Congress passed a similar resolution in June, but Trump dismissed that vote as "poorly timed and meaningless."

The White House has argued that efforts to limit Trump's authority would weaken Washington as it seeks to pressure Tehran.

Democrats and a small number of Republicans say the opposite: that Congress must reclaim its constitutional role over decisions of war and peace.

item.title: WHO aims to reduce drowning deaths by 35pc by 2035
item.description:
Although most of deaths from drowning are preventable, more than 300,000 people die from drowning around the world every year.

As drowning has long remained one of the most neglected public health issues, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the United Nations now consider it a global priority.

To that end, WHO released the Global Strategy for Drowning Prevention last year (2025), aiming to reduce drowning deaths worldwide by 35 per cent by 2035.

Caroline Lukaszyk, Technical Officer, Unintentional Injury at World Health Organization, said WHO will work closely with member states to achieve the target of reducing drowning deaths by 35 per cent by 2035. Member states will also receive the necessary support to implement effective interventions.

To help member states formulate effective policies on drowning prevention, WHO will present a guidance document. An international conference for that purpose began on Wednesday in Accra, the capital of Ghana.

Representatives from Bangladesh, India, the United States, Ghana, Uganda and Vietnam, including non-governmental organisations and media professionals, are attending the conference. These six countries, including Bangladesh, record relatively high numbers of drowning deaths.

Two sessions were held on the opening day. The event has been organised by the World Health Organization with support from Bloomberg Philanthropies. A press conference was also held by WHO in the evening.

At the press briefing, Caroline Lukaszyk said drowning occurs in every country in the world. Unfortunately, however, it has not received the attention it deserves. “So many deaths are simply unacceptable. They must be prevented,” she said, adding that the World Health Organization aims to reduce global drowning deaths by at least 35 per cent by 2035.

Lukaszyk said that while some countries have policies or laws aimed at preventing drowning, most do not. Even where such measures exist, their effectiveness often remains uncertain.

Speaking at the same press briefing, Kofi Mengaka Nyarko, WHO Regional Adviser for Africa, said many drowning deaths around the world go unrecorded.

He added that developing a strong drowning surveillance and data system is essential for preventing deaths, noting that many countries still lack such systems. Drowning has become a major public health concern across many African countries.

According to WHO's global strategy published last year, more than 300,000 people died from drowning worldwide in 2021. One in four victims was under the age of five, while nearly half were younger than 29. More than 90 per cent of drowning deaths occurred in low- and middle-income countries.

For many of these countries, drowning is not only a public health issue but also a major development and economic challenge. In some countries, the economic cost of drowning is estimated to be as high as 3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) annually.

The strategy also highlights that drowning is preventable. Effective measures include safe supervision of children, protective barriers around water bodies, swimming and water safety education, rescue and first aid training, and ensuring the safety of water transport.

WHO first identified drowning as a public health issue in 2002. In 2003, a drowning prevention project was launched in Bangladesh. In 2014, WHO published its first global report on drowning.

In 2021, the United Nations General Assembly adopted its first-ever resolution on drowning prevention and declared 25 July as World Drowning Prevention Day. In 2023, the World Health Assembly also adopted a separate resolution on the issue.

Reports by the United Nations and several international organisations have pointed out that Bangladesh lacks accurate and regular reporting on drowning deaths.

However, various estimates suggest that more than 18,000 people die from drowning in the country every year. Of them, around 11,000 are children under the age of five.

Earlier on Wednesday, representatives from organisations working on drowning prevention in the United States, India, Vietnam and Uganda shared their experiences during the morning session.

Tessa Clemens, a representative of the CDC Foundation in US, said that drowning deaths are concentrated in 11 US states, with Alaska recording the highest burden. She noted that climate change has increased the frequency of extreme rainfall and flooding, contributing to a higher risk of drowning.

Meghendra Banerjee, Chief of Programs at Child in Need Institute in India, said drowning is still not treated as a major public health issue despite the large number of lives it claims.

He noted, however, that the Government of West Bengal has recently instructed district administrations to report drowning deaths. According to him, this initiative indicates that the government has become more attentive to drowning prevention.

item.title: Students spread message against human trafficking, migrant smuggling
item.description:
"People are not for sale." Although the sentence is short, it carries a powerful message. Using this simple phrase, Nusrat Jahan, a ninth-grade student from Narayanganj, wrote an essay and message on human trafficking and migrant smuggling.

Just like Nusrat, 870 students from across the country submitted essays expressing their thoughts and proposed solutions on human trafficking and migrant smuggling. Among them, 31 finalists received awards and certificates, while six students emerged as winners across two competition categories.

Literary researcher and essayist Professor Syed Azizul Haque and National Book Centre director Afsana Begum presented the awards to the winners at a ceremony held at the BRAC Centre in Mohakhali today, Thursday (23 July), reports a press release.

The competition was judged by writer, researcher and migration expert Afsan Chowdhury, journalist Rajib Noor, and fiction writer Kizzy Tahnin.

As part of a public awareness campaign to prevent human trafficking and migrant smuggling, the BRAC Migration Programme conducted awareness activities at educational institutions across the country. Students, teachers and parents attended the event, jointly organised by the Australian Border Force and the BRAC Migration Programme.

The essay competition aimed to help school, college and university students identify the signs of human trafficking and migrant smuggling, raise awareness of the dangers of irregular migration by sea, and highlight the importance of safe, regular and legal migration.

The competition was held in two categories: Class Eight to college level and university level.

In the senior category, Niloy Biswas of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology was crowned champion, while Mohammad Fahad Hossain Fahim of Bangladesh Agricultural University was named runner-up.

In the junior category, Nadhratun Nayeem Taqwa, a ninth-grade student of Khurushkul High School in Cox's Bazar, won the championship. The joint first runners-up were Sadia Salma, a tenth-grade student of Shaheed Azizul Haque Girls' Madrasa in Teknaf, and Arafat Shaheen Kamal, a tenth-grade student of Sabrang High School in Teknaf.

Sejuti Akter Ayesha, a ninth-grade student of Pirujali Adarsha Bidyalaya in Gazipur, secured third place in this category.

Speaking as the chief guest at the prize-giving ceremony, Professor Syed Azizul Haque said, “Traffickers succeed in this country because our poverty in education is far greater than our poverty in income.”

“Those who fall victim to trafficking and endure unimaginable suffering are not the only ones affected; it is an issue concerning the entire nation. Preventing trafficking is everyone's responsibility. The messages conveyed through participants in this essay competition can help raise awareness across society,” he added.

Special guest Afsana Begum reflected on the hardships she witnessed among many Bangladeshis during her time living in Malaysia, saying that greater public awareness could protect many people from falling into danger.

Safi Rahman Khan, director of BRAC's Education, Skills Development and Migration Programme, said the fight against human trafficking and migrant smuggling is fundamentally about ensuring people's right to safe and dignified migration.

“We have been working with students for many years and have seen that wherever they become involved, positive change follows. This essay competition was organised to raise awareness of these issues among young people,” he said.

Shariful Islam Hasan, associate director of BRAC, said, “Bangladesh is the world's sixth-largest source of migrant workers. Yet those who go abroad are often referred to as kamlas (manual labourers), even though the country's economy relies heavily on their labour.”

“Their lives and struggles are absent from our textbooks. We wanted to hear students' perspectives on this issue and involve them in the discussion. This was about much more than a competition or prizes; our goal was to make students think seriously about this important issue,” he added.

Junior category runner-up Arafat Shaheen, a tenth-grade student from Teknaf, spoke about the widespread problem of human trafficking in his area.

“In Teknaf, human trafficking and abduction have become alarmingly common. People are kidnapped for ransom, trafficked and tortured. Videos of the abuse are sent to their families to extort money. Families often end up selling their property to pay the ransom. These crimes have become almost normal in Teknaf. Finding a solution is urgent,” he said.

Mobasshira Anjum, a student of YWCA Higher Secondary Girls' School in Dhaka and one of the competition participants, said, “While gathering information and researching for my essay, I realised for the first time just how widespread human trafficking and migrant smuggling are, and how devastating their consequences can be.”

At the event, Mannan Chhaiyal, who recently returned from a cyber scam centre in Cambodia, and Ong Ong Jewel, a survivor of human trafficking from Cox's Bazar, shared their harrowing experiences and urged the public to remain vigilant against human trafficking and migrant smuggling.

item.title: Speaker to return two days ahead of schedule, fueling speculation over President’s resignation
item.description:
Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed is set to return home from Thailand tomorrow on Friday afternoon, two days ahead of the scheduled time.

Parliament Secretariat sources say he was initially scheduled to return next Sunday, but the schedule has been moved forward.

The decision has intensified speculation over the possible resignation of President Md Shahabuddin, following reports that he may step down soon. Under Bangladesh's Constitution, the president submits a resignation letter to the Speaker. If the president resigns, the Speaker assumes the president's duties until a new President is elected.

According to Parliament Secretariat sources, Hafiz travelled to Bangkok on 19 July for medical treatment and was scheduled to return on 26 July. The revised schedule was confirmed on Thursday.

In a programme circulated by the BNP for its senior leaders on Thursday evening, the party said the Speaker is expected to arrive in Dhaka at 12:40pm on Friday on a Thai Airways flight from Thailand.

The Constitution states, if the office of the President becomes vacant or if the President is unable to discharge the functions of his office on account of absence, illness or any other cause, the Speaker shall discharge those functions until a President is elected or until the President resumes the functions of his office, as the case may be.

It also requires that a new president be elected within 90 days if the office falls vacant due to resignation.

Amid the discussions regarding the President’s resignation, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmad, in response to a question on the matter after a cabinet meeting at the Secretariat this afternoon, said, "Wait until Friday."

item.title: What has happened so far in India's protests demanding education minister's resignation
item.description:
INDIA-POLITICS-EDUCATION-PROTEST

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has promised swift justice in the NEET examination paper leak cases. However, the student protest group Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has rejected the assurance, insisting that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan must resign.

The opposition has also dismissed the Prime Minister's appeal, deciding that Parliament will not discuss the issue unless Pradhan steps down.

Congress MP KC Venugopal told reporters on Thursday that opposition leaders had informed Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla that they would boycott any discussion until the Education Minister was dismissed. So, there appears to be little prospect of an immediate resolution to the student movement.

However, the opposition's position is not unanimous. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) have not joined the boycott. Venugopal said all other opposition parties remain united in demanding Pradhan's resignation.

The protesters and the opposition received a major boost on Thursday when veteran Gandhian activist Anna Hazare publicly endorsed their demands.

Hazare, who led the landmark 2011 anti-corruption hunger strike that forced the then Congress-led UPA government to enact the Lokpal law, had remained silent until now.

On Wednesday, he wrote a letter to Prime Minister Modi. According to The Indian Express, Hazare wrote that the government will not fall if Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns. Rather, it will enable the government to function more responsibly and play a more effective role.

Describing reports of police violence against protesters as "deeply painful," Hazare urged the Prime Minister to engage directly with demonstrators.

"Talk to the protesters. Listen to them patiently. Build an atmosphere of trust and confidence, and seek a solution through constructive dialogue."

No such initiative has yet been announced. Nevertheless, the government has once again expressed its willingness to negotiate. Union Minister Jitendra Singh told CJP leaders on Thursday that the government was prepared to hold talks at any time and at any place convenient for them.

The protests also continued to paralyse Parliament on Thursday.

Repeated disruptions by opposition lawmakers forced both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha to adjourn several times throughout the day.

Opposition MPs staged demonstrations inside the Parliament complex, while members of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) organised counter-protests.

Leaders of the ruling coalition accused Rahul Gandhi of provoking young people for narrow political gains.

Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also joined the opposition protest, carrying a large banner reading "Dismiss Pradhan" in English and Hindi.

The opposition chanted, ‘Save lives, stop NEET.’ The ruling coalition responded with slogans including, ‘Don't mislead the youth, Rahul Gandhi, wake up.’

At one point, lawmakers from both sides confronted each other face-to-face. CPM MP John Brittas was seen snatching a poster from BJP MP Arun Singh. Security personnel intervened, forming a human barrier to prevent the confrontation from escalating while slogan-shouting continued.

The government told both houses that it was ready for a debate on NEET and the education system. The opposition refused, insisting there would be no discussion until Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.

Both houses were first adjourned until noon, then until 2:00 pm, before being suspended for the rest of the day. Parliament has now remained effectively paralysed for four consecutive days.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kirren Rijiju said in the Lok Sabha that the government is ready to discuss the issue whenever, however, and for as long as the opposition wants—but discussions cannot be subject to preconditions.

Modi's message and Rahul Gandhi's response

Prime Minister Modi addressed the protesting students early Thursday morning through a post on X in both Hindi and English.

He wrote, “Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps in this regard. This continues our series of steps for safeguarding the interests of students. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared.”

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi responded shortly afterward on X, directly tagging the Prime Minister's post.

He wrote, “You are the one who has harmed the future of our youth the most. You allowed and encouraged the total capture and destruction of our education system - and protected every person responsible for it.

The students’ demands are clear: 1. Sack Dharmendra Pradhan. 2. Apologise to the students. 3. Take action against those who assaulted them.

Almost simultaneously, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) reposted Modi's message with a brief response:

"Dharmendra Pradhan must resign."

Clashes at Jantar Mantar

Late Wednesday night, police and protesters clashed in three separate confrontations at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.

Several protesters and police officers were injured.

Police used batons and tear gas, and filed First Information Reports (FIRs) against those detained.

CJP leaders blamed both the BJP and the Delhi Police for the violence.

CJP leader Abhijit Dipke told reporters, "We've been protesting at Jantar Mantar for over a month without any trouble. This is the first time violence has occurred. The BJP and the police are behind it."

He alleged that, acting on BJP instructions, police had brought in hired troublemakers to provoke violence.

"Truckloads of stones were brought in. BJP supporters threw them. Their aim is to discredit the CJP."

Metro stations remain closed

Delhi Metro authorities kept 16 metro stations closed throughout Wednesday and continued the closures on Thursday morning.

The affected stations are located around Connaught Place and nearby areas, causing severe inconvenience to commuters.

Some passengers staged anti-government demonstrations at several stations.

The Supreme Court Bar Association has urged the Chief Justice of India to intervene, arguing that the closures prevented many lawyers from reaching court on time and caused widespread disruption.

Chief Justice Surya Kant has assured the association that the matter will be considered.

item.title: BGB foils BSF push-in attempt at Chuadanga border
item.description:
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has successfully foiled an attempt by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) to illegally push five individuals into Bangladeshi territory at the Chuadanga border early Tuesday.

According to a press release issued by the BGB’s Chuadanga Battalion (6 BGB), the incident occurred around 4:00am near border pillar 76/4-S, under the jurisdiction of the Darshana Border Outpost (BOP).

The BGB reported that members of the Gede camp under the 32 BSF Battalion attempted to facilitate the illegal entry of five unidentified individuals, including one man, three women, and one child into Bangladesh.

A BGB patrol team immediately detected the movement and blocked the individuals from entering the country. The push-in attempt forced the group to remain near the border's barbed-wire fence.

Following a firm stance by the BGB, the BSF was eventually compelled to take the individuals back into Indian territory.

Major Towasin Habib Hasan, Acting Commander of the Chuadanga Battalion (6 BGB) stated that the BGB remains on high alert and is fully prepared to prevent any form of illegal intrusion or violation of border laws.

He emphasised that the force continues to perform its duties with professionalism and vigilance to ensure border security and maintain peace in the region.
